findings.summary: Settle-to-zero departure posts an adjustment without any network-state gate, even on closed, closing, suspended or administrator-required networks, breaking the certified final export checksum after closure.
findings.note: Network-state gate refuses settlement postings after closure, during suspension and when an administrator is required.

findings.summary: The decimals guard (LedgerSeq > 0) is checked only when a change is requested, so a decimals change scheduled with notice takes effect after postings exist and reinterprets all persisted amounts permanently.
findings.note: Scale changes refused at creation boundary; scheduled-change bypass regression covered. Historical databases with already-scheduled scale changes still require migration policy.

findings.summary: A re-review posts a reversal on a trade that another live (serial) dispute holds as disputed, leaving a posting_pending dispute that can never post or close, or an open dispute on a reversed trade that cannot be withdrawn and no longer blocks closure or departure.
findings.note: Re-review posting refused while another live dispute owns the transaction.

findings.summary: ResolveDispute and RetryDisputePosting post reversals in an administrator-required network because reverse() checks only Suspended(), unlike DecideReReview which applies the full gate.
findings.note: networkOpenErr gates reverse; PR69 adds entry-point regression, independently mutation-tested in this review.

findings.summary: The expiry sweep pages the oldest N expired proposals across all networks and skips frozen ones, so 500+ elapsed proposals in frozen networks starve every other network's expiry.
findings.note: Frozen networks excluded before the bounded sweep; healthy expiry does not starve.

findings.summary: Departure cancels only one page of 500 open proposals, leaving the rest proposed with a departed party and holding the counterparty's reservation until expiry.
findings.note: Departure cancels proposals beyond the first 500.

findings.summary: Closure commits closed status in one unit and writes the final export in later units; if the export fails once, the closure is never listed again so no final checksum is ever recorded.
findings.note: Closure with an absent final checksum remains eligible for retry.

findings.summary: OperatorSetDualControl writes policy version effective+1, which collides with an already scheduled future version, so the operator cannot change the threshold while any policy change is pending.
findings.note: Operator changes preserve scheduled policy values and allocate the next revision.

findings.summary: Reversal transactions posted by a dispute decision, retry or re-review have no audit event targeting the reversal id; only the dispute is the target.
findings.note: Reversal-target audit events and ledger postings share the transaction.

findings.summary: ExpirePendingAdjustments writes status changes and audit events into frozen networks, whereas proposal expiry and closure finalisation skip frozen networks.
findings.note: Frozen pending adjustments excluded before bounded selection.

findings.summary: FR-005 and GOV-004 are marked built although creation-time decimals immutability is unimplemented, and TestPolicyChanges asserts the non-conforming behaviour.
findings.note: Current tests enforce scale immutability; remediation record amended FR-005/GOV-004. DOM-031/DAT-049 remain separately qualified.

findings.summary: Case-variant duplicate JSON keys pass the duplicate check (last spelling wins) and wrongly-cased field names are accepted instead of refused as unknown.
findings.note: Canonical JSON field names reject case aliases; strict body tests remain.

findings.summary: A token restricted to one network lists the person's other tokens (with other network ids), revokes them, and changes the person-wide time zone.
findings.note: Network-bound tokens cannot manage person-wide tokens/preferences.

findings.summary: The replay cache is keyed only by person+key, so a read-only token (or demoted admin) replays a cached write response such as a plaintext invitation token.
findings.note: Replay reauthorizes scope, role, MFA, break-glass expiry and current membership.

findings.summary: A break-glass grant-admin administrator is refused by every web admin page and by API adminOnly pre-checks, while the service accepts them.
findings.note: Adapters use live effective admin authority including authorized break-glass grants.

findings.summary: GET /admin/consistency-checks/{id} and GET /admin/policy are authorised only by the adapter role check, so an admin without the mandatory second factor can read them.
findings.note: Administrator reads/navigation enforce the currently required MFA.

findings.summary: POST /logout ignores a failed session revocation, reports 'You are signed out.' and clears the cookie while the server session stays valid.
findings.note: Failed server revocation does not clear retryable session or claim success.

findings.summary: Credit-limit and policy ETags omit the override/expiry and scheduled policy changes, so a stale If-Match succeeds and silently undoes another admin's change.
findings.note: Conditional writes include effective, pending, override and expiry state, with atomic service recheck.

findings.summary: Runtime 423 network-frozen, 429, 503 busy and some 413/415 statuses are not documented in openapi.yaml, so kin-openapi validation rejects them.
findings.note: OpenAPI response declarations are fixed. Original finding lines133–135 also require four absent problem-code catalogue rows. PR84 supplies those rows; its regression fails on exact baseline main and passes on the candidate. The unmerged candidate is not counted as integrated.

findings.summary: GET /network/policy-log returns every version and GET /challenges up to 200 rows, both with next_cursor null, ignoring limit, cursor and status.
findings.note: Bounded signed pagination for policy logs and challenges.

findings.summary: /n/{slug}/join tells any signed-in person whether a slug exists and shows the name of an invitation-only network, while other /n/{slug} pages answer 404.
findings.note: Invitation-only networks remain opaque to outsiders; public join modes retained.

findings.summary: Sections hidden from a suspended or departed member's navigation still answer 200 by URL.
findings.note: Navigation reflects readable suspended/departed sections.

findings.summary: A re-review decision posting a reversal is recorded on first submit with no review step, and dual-control 'Approve and post' also posts without a review screen.
findings.note: Re-review and dual-control approval use signed reviewed confirmation, rechecking live state.

findings.summary: Frozen-network notice and admin overview last-check line display escaped <time datetime=...> markup as text.
findings.note: Notice times render as time elements rather than escaped markup.

findings.summary: Custom qs (url.QueryEscape) inside href is escaped again by html/template, so the double-encoded next fails SafeNext and invitation sign-in lands on '/'.
findings.note: Rendered invitation/login/register links retain one correctly escaped local return path.

findings.summary: /static/*, /robots.txt and /favicon.ico are Cache-Control: public yet carry a fresh Set-Cookie cm_csrf pre-login CSRF secret.
findings.note: Cacheable public assets issue no CSRF cookies.

findings.summary: Path ids reach the store unvalidated; SQL is parameterised so not exploitable, but SEC-024 requires rejection before any database call.
findings.note: Record identifiers rejected before repository calls after authorization, preserving opaque failures.

findings.summary: A person who must change their password can still load '/' and '/join/{token}' instead of being redirected.
findings.note: Home and invitation entry points enforce forced password change.

findings.summary: invalid-body problem detail echoes Go internals and several reads ignore unknown query parameters.
findings.note: Decoder messages hide Go internals; unknown/malformed queries refused.

findings.summary: OpenAPI declares an optional Idempotency-Key on POST /tokens but the route ignores it, so a retry with the same key mints a second credential.
findings.note: POST/tokens correctly documents no Idempotency-Key support; token secrets are never cached. Canonical API-066 SHOULD remains design guidance, not a runtime replay promise.

findings.summary: The web reference shown to users is a second random id unrelated to the access-log request_id, and the API stores a client-chosen X-Request-Id in audit events.
findings.note: Edge and adapter request identifiers are correlated; untrusted client identifiers do not replace the server audit identifier.

findings.summary: API tokens and session ids are stored as plain unsalted, unkeyed SHA-256 whereas the spec requires a salted or keyed hash.
findings.note: hashToken still uses plain SHA-256, so API-009 salted/keyed-hash wording is unmet. Tokens contain 256 random bits; credential format migration and key/salt lookup compatibility need explicit design. No unapproved token revocation or format change.

findings.summary: With backup-encryption-key set, the pre-migration gate runs integrity_check on the .db.enc ciphertext, so circula migrate and serve (migrate-mode=auto) can never migrate an encrypted deployment.
findings.note: Encrypted pre-migration backups decrypted before database integrity verification.

findings.summary: Break-glass 'no lasting changes' rule (requireLasting) covers only about 10 methods, so a break-glass admin can post adjustments, approve dual-control requests immediately, raise limits, reset passwords, reverse trades and decide disputes.
findings.note: DEC-014 remains unresolved. Current original PoC re-run separately; no break-glass/governance policy changed.

findings.summary: Second-factor throttle is renewable by one failure at expiry and is shared with session-only DisableMFA, so a stolen session keeps the owner out of MFA sign-in indefinitely.
findings.note: Session-side operations cannot renew/consume the owner sign-in MFA budget.

findings.summary: require-mfa-admins is not applied to admin powers reached through requireDecider, so an admin without a second factor resolves disputes and decides challenges.
findings.note: requireDecider enforces admin MFA; PR69 service-entry regression independently mutation-tested.

findings.summary: Erasure leaves the member's challenge text (challenges.reason) and the login in 'recover: <login>' throttle rows.
findings.note: Recovery and sign-in throttle families erased, including Unicode/IP variants. Challenge reasons still survive; SEC-014/018 retention policy unresolved.

findings.summary: DeleteThrottleFamily compares a Go byte length with SQLite character substr, so per-address throttle rows of non-ASCII logins are never removed.
findings.note: SQLite character-length cleanup replaces mismatched Go-byte length and respects literal prefixes.

findings.summary: Restore resurrects sessions and API tokens revoked after the backup (and, by trace, closed break-glass sessions), and the documented remedy (password change) leaves tokens valid.
findings.note: Restore invalidates bearer sessions/tokens and break-glass credentials before swap. Password/recovery-code/invitation state still reflects the backup; separate operational limitation.

findings.summary: Backup schedule and retention trust the timestamp in backup file names, so one future-dated backup stops scheduled backups for years and is always retained.
findings.note: Cadence exclusion is fixed in main. Retention exclusion and clock-anomaly logging are independently source-reviewed and regression-verified in PR84, but remain unmerged while required provider CI is incomplete. Keep this historical finding partial on main.

findings.summary: circula dual-control fails with 'conflict: duplicate record' while a policy change waits out its notice because both use version in-force+1.
findings.note: Same correction as A1-08.

findings.summary: Docs say rotating circula-web.key signs everyone out, but sessions are unsigned DB tokens that survive and no mass session revocation exists.
findings.note: Explicit audited revoke-sessions command and corrected key-rotation documentation; no claim that key rotation alone revokes opaque sessions.

findings.summary: Migration static check flags only DROP TABLE/COLUMN and DELETE FROM, missing UPDATE entries/audit_events and DROP TRIGGER.
findings.note: Protected append-only UPDATE/REPLACE/UPSERT and DROP TRIGGER checked, with lexical/comment/exemption regressions.

findings.summary: Hourly scheduled verification writes a consistency_runs row every run (and audit events on failure/recovery), contrary to the accepted read-only rule.
findings.note: Scheduled ledger verification is read-only while maintaining in-memory freeze/thaw behavior.

findings.summary: Manifest/record/anchor writers use a fixed <path>.tmp with os.WriteFile which follows symlinks, allowing file clobber when backing up into a shared directory.
findings.note: Manifest/record/anchor writers use unpredictable exclusively-created files. Plaintext snapshot staging residual is NEW-01, handled separately.

findings.summary: Per-member credit-limit cuts take effect at once although the policy table requires GOV-003 notice, sidestepping the 14-day notice on default-limit cuts.
findings.note: Per-member limit cuts still apply immediately. GOV-003/default-policy notice versus per-member notice requires owner decision; no financial-rule change.

findings.summary: Authentication throttling limits are constants, not operator settings, although OPS-008 lists them as required settings and it is marked built.
findings.note: Operator authentication settings bounded, validated and wired into service.

findings.summary: Erasure blanks every inbox body in the network containing the display name as a substring, so a 1-character name wipes other members' notifications via self-service erasure.
findings.note: Notification erasure targets exact resource relationships, preserving unrelated name substrings.

findings.summary: Erased values remain in -wal frames after the normal PASSIVE checkpoint; the RB-003 test passes only because it forces TRUNCATE.
findings.note: PASSIVE checkpoint can retain erased plaintext in WAL frames. Forced TRUNCATE policy and concurrency/availability consequences unresolved; secure_delete alone does not prove historical-page removal.

findings.summary: A schema_migrations row with version <= 0 makes every open panic (all[v-1]) instead of failing cleanly.
findings.note: Nonpositive migration metadata refuses cleanly instead of indexing out of bounds.

findings.summary: Forbidden-name scan runs tar -tzf on .zip archives, so the Windows archive is never inspected.
findings.note: ZIP-specific listing/extraction implemented. This review independently ran clean and forbidden-name ZIP fixtures; exits 0 and 1 respectively.

findings.summary: Docs say '15 min doubling to 24 h' but code locks a fixed 15 min (throttleMax).
findings.note: PR75. Existing focused throttle/recovery tests pass; independent source/documentation review approves. SEC-006 normative wording is retained with an explicit implementation/deviation note; no owner decision or authentication policy changed.

findings.summary: break-glass grant-admin -login is not normalised for case, unlike every other operator command.
findings.note: Break-glass target login normalized consistently with sign-in.

findings.summary: admin create-operator is audited as the new person registering themself; nothing marks it as an operator action.
findings.note: Operator registration audited as the operator, rather than self-registration.

findings.summary: Erasure drops only the erased person's in-memory artefacts; another administrator's full export made before the erasure stays downloadable for up to 24 h.
findings.note: Erasure invalidates affected archives and running exports; admitted downloads pinned/revoked safely.
